blocks.text: AN OPEN COLLECTION THESE RECORDS CAME FROM

Europeana is not a museum. It gathers the catalogues of European institutions and publishes their descriptions under a single open licence, while each item keeps its own rights statement. The institutions behind these records have their own cards.
111 records are held for this collection and 24 are listed here — the ones its own records tie to something biblical, audited first. The rest are in the research corpus, not on this page.
What we hold for this collection.
The Black Obelisk of Shalmaneser III

KU Leuven. Glass slides art history. Université de Louvain, between 1839 and 1939. Photographer unknown. Added information on slide. Style: Mesopotamian art (Neo-Assyrian art). Original location:Mesopotamia, Assyria, Kalhu (Iraq, Nimrud). Creation/Building: 825 BC. Technique/Material: Limestone. Current location: United Kingdom, London, British Museum. EuroPhot. Archaeology. Antiquity. Sculpture. Relief. EuroPhot.…
Its reach, and its limit. Names Jehu's tribute; depicted kneeling figure may be a representative.

Folio from the Book of Numbers and Deuteronomy (R963), written in Greek with ink on papyrus; made in Egypt and dated to the second or third century AD. The text follows the Septuagint, or Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible. The manuscript is the earliest dated book in the Biblical Papyrus collection and until the discovery of the Dead Sea Scrolls (1947) was the earliest surviving copy of any portion of the Bible.…
